item.title: Grip & Racket Basics
item.description:
1. Overview

Everything in badminton starts with the grip.

Whether you are playing a clear, smash, drop shot, net shot, drive, lift, or serve, your grip controls:

  • power
  • accuracy
  • racket angle
  • deception
  • finger control
  • injury prevention

Many recreational players struggle with advanced shots not because they are weak, but because they hold the racket incorrectly.

This lesson should be revisited regularly, even after you move to intermediate skills.

item.title: Ready Position, Split Step & Court Preparation
item.description:
1. Overview

Badminton is often called the fastest racket sport in the world.

At higher levels, players don’t wait until they see the shuttle before they start moving.

Instead, they prepare before the opponent hits the shuttle.

This preparation consists of three simple but extremely important concepts:

  • Ready Position
  • Split Step
  • Recovery

Every movement you make on court starts with these three.

Whether you are playing:

  • a clear
  • a smash
  • a drop shot
  • a net shot
  • a defensive block

you will always repeat the same movement cycle.

item.title: The First Step – Starting Every Movement
item.description:
1. Overview

Many beginners believe fast footwork comes from moving their legs quickly.

In reality, great footwork starts with one correct first step.

Professional players don’t waste movement. They don’t take unnecessary steps or run around the court.

Instead, they generate explosive movement from the ground and let one powerful first step take them towards the shuttle.

This lesson teaches the foundation of every movement you’ll make on a badminton court.
